full_judgment:
8. The learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellants submits that the 1st appellate Court acted illegally in reversing the judgment without assigning sufficient and cogent reasons, that trial Court, by cogent reason decreed the plaintiffs claim for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. It is further submitted that the learned lower appellate Court misapplied the provision of section 28(2) of the Registration Act in disregard of the fact that kabala Ext. A was registered fraudulently at Baliakandi Sub-Registry Office by including therein a fictitious piece of land of Baliakandi police station though the kabala land lies within the jurisdiction of Pangsha Sub-Registrar Office and that the appellants being not party to the said deed are competent to challenge it as invalid inasmuch as it was a fraud on registration. The learned Advocate continued to urge that the 1st appellate Court committed error in fact and law in not holding that the kabala Ext. 2 of 1947 by plaintiffs predecessor Md. Rawshan Ali Shaikh in favour of his step brothers defendants No. 7 Akbar Ali and deceased minor Ajibar was not acted upon; inasmuch as no consideration passed from Akbar and Ajibar for which original kabala was returned to Roushan Ali and he continued to remain in possession thereon and accordingly the original kabala was produced during trial from the custody of the plaintiffs. It is further urged that 1st appellate Court misdirected himself in finding possession in favour of the defendant in quite disregard of the fact that in defendants kabala the homestead dag has been mentioned as cultivable Nal land though in fact the plaintiffs were living thereon. The learned Advocate further urged that the impugned judgment is not the proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the 1st appellate Court did not advert to the reasoning's assigned by the trial Court in support of his findings. 

 16. The learned Advocate for the appellants has urged with emphasis that the impugned judgment passed by the Additional District Judge is not the proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the object of rule 31 of Order XLI has not been complied with. This contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants appears to be well founded. The object of rule 31 of Order XLI CPC is to see that a Judge does not act callously or even mechanically its purpose is to put the Judge on the right track and to the extent rule of procedure can do it, to see that he acts judicially. It enables the High Court to judge whether the 1st appellate Court had independently considered the case with a consciousness of relevant points which arose for adjudication. It is also to afford the parties opportunity of knowing the grounds of decision to enable them to exercise the right of second appeal and to enable the High Court in Second Appeal to judge whether lower appellate Court has properly appreciated and decided the case. Appellate judgment reversing the judgment of trial Court should be adequate and satisfactory. It must contain definite findings on the question involved and must give reasons for reversing the decision of the trial Court. In fact judgment of reversal may often need a little more discussions of facts, evidence and points involved in the case so as to embody in it convincing reasons for reversing the findings of the Courts of 1st instance. It should cover almost en- tire ground covered by the judgment appealed from. It must express opinion on all points on which the lower court has based its conclusion. It is not necessary for lower appellate Court to mention each and every particular item of evidence in its judgment provided it is clear upon reading of the judgment itself that all relevant evidence has been substantially considered by the lower appellate Court. The appellate Judgment may not meet all reasons given in the judgment of trial Court, while setting it aside. The principles had not been followed by the 1st appellate Court inasmuch as in some places appellate Court grossly misread the evidence. The trial Court discussed the evidence on the point of possession but the 1st appellate Court did not consider it at all. Regarding production of original deed (Ext. 2) from the custody of plaintiff's appellants, the 1st appellate Court observed that widow of Roushan Ali was married to Akbar Ali but in support of this contention there is no iota of evidence on record. The widow of Roushan Ali was examined on commission and she denied this suggestion stoutly. The trial Court dealt with the matter in detail but the learned 1st appellate Court did not advert to it in its judgment. 

 18. Thus, having considered the entire materials on record and the facts, circumstances and the legal principle referred to above I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment of the 1st appellate Court is not the proper judgment of reversal and as such it cannot be sustained in law.
